text: You’ve found the perfect parking spot, but you’re in a rush. Every second counts when you’re trying to make it on time.
You grab your wallet, pull out a nice crisp bill, and approach the meter. But wait… it only wants coins or plastic.
Why can’t this simple machine just take your money? You just want to park and get on with your day, but the meter refuses to cooperate.
It feels like a conspiracy, but the reason is simpler: bills are expensive for machines. Verifying authenticity, dispensing change, preventing jams – it all requires complex machinery.
Coins are simple: they just need to be counted. Cards? They offload all the complex money handling, like verification and change, to banks.
So the next time you’re fumbling for change, remember: it’s not to annoy you. It’s an invisible system of efficiency, making sure your parking meter stays simple and functional.
